body.statement: Under the present certificate grammar and checker, the answer to the proof-carrying compiler question is negative.  For every integer \(k\geq 1\), there is an explicit finite acyclic target grounding and compact equality-query description whose combined pre-incidence input size is \(O(k)\), whose target ground graph is edgeless and hence has treewidth \(w=0\), and which has binary variables \(X_1,\ldots,X_{k+1}\), no intervention, target event \(B=\{X_1=X_{k+1}\}\), a fair supported row at \(X_1\), and the unsupported binary row \(rstar\) at \(X_{k+1}\).  The row \(rstar\) is directly event-relevant and the replayed target polynomial is the nontrivial constant \(F=1/2\), while the mandated \(Ictx\) contains exactly \(2^k\) event-consistent complete target-assignment records.  Consequently, every compiler that outputs an \(Ictx\) accepted by \(Check\) has time and output length \(\Omega(2^k)\).  Thus no bound polynomial in the explicit grounding size and exponential only in \(w\) is possible for this exhaustive assignment-level grammar.  This conclusion does not rule out a width-sensitive compiler after replacement of \(Ictx\) and \(Check\) by a compact circuit-level incidence grammar and checker.
body.proof_tex:
Fix an integer \(k\geq 1\).  We construct the promised instance.  Take a fixed finite relational schema with two binary endogenous attribute types, called \(A\) and \(C\), and take the relational causal graph to have no directed edges.  Let the source list contain a grounding with one isolated node of type \(A\), whose rational source law assigns probability \(1/2\) to each binary outcome.  The corresponding parent context is the empty tuple, it has positive source probability, and hence its conditional row is recovered in \(K\).  Let the target grounding consist of isolated binary nodes \(X_1,\ldots,X_{k+1}\).  Nodes \(X_1,\ldots,X_k\) have type \(A\) in that supported context, whereas \(X_{k+1}\) has type \(C\) in a type--context key absent from every source grounding; designate that key by \(rstar\).  Choose the schema so that these are the only target-relevant type--context keys.  It follows that \(rstar\) is the unique unsupported target-relevant key.  Use the empty intervention and the compactly described event
\[
 B_k:=\{x\in\{0,1\}^{k+1}:x_1=x_{k+1}\}.
\]
All domains are finite, as required by \(\texttt{ass:finite-domains}\).  The target ground graph is edgeless, so it is acyclic by construction and satisfies \(\texttt{ass:acyclic-groundings}\).  The family of singleton bags \(\{X_j\}\), connected in any tree, is a tree decomposition: every vertex occurs in a bag, there is no edge to cover, and the bags containing any fixed vertex form a connected singleton subtree.  Its width is \(1-1=0\), so \(w=0\).

The schema, graph, and source description have constant size.  The ordered target node list has \(k+1\) entries and an empty edge list, and the equality event is specified by the indices \(1\) and \(k+1\).  Thus, in the fixed canonical encoding underlying \(\texttt{def:certificate-grammar}\), the combined input before materialization of \(Ictx\) has size \(O(k)\).

By the supported source row and \(\texttt{ass:type-sharing}\), every occurrence \(X_j\), \(1\leq j\leq k\), has conditional mass function
\[
 p_A(x_j)=\frac12,
 \qquad x_j\in\{0,1\}.
\]
For the unsupported binary key \(rstar\), write its shared row as
\[
 p_q(z)=(1-q)^{1-z}q^z,
 \qquad z\in\{0,1\},\quad q\in[0,1].
\]
Because the target graph has no edges and the intervention is empty, the truncated-factorization replay specified in the definition of \(F\) is
\[
 F_k(q)
 =\sum_{\substack{x\in\{0,1\}^{k+1}\\x_1=x_{k+1}}}
   \left(\prod_{j=1}^{k}\frac12\right)
   (1-q)^{1-x_{k+1}}q^{x_{k+1}}.
\]
When \(x_{k+1}=0\), the event forces \(x_1=0\), while \(x_2,\ldots,x_k\) may be chosen freely.  There are therefore \(2^{k-1}\) such terms, whose sum is
\[
 2^{k-1}2^{-k}(1-q)=\frac{1-q}{2}.
\]
When \(x_{k+1}=1\), the event forces \(x_1=1\), again leaving \(2^{k-1}\) choices, and these terms sum to
\[
 2^{k-1}2^{-k}q=\frac q2.
\]
Consequently
\[
 F_k(q)=\frac{1-q}{2}+\frac q2=\frac12
 \quad\text{for every }q\in[0,1].
\]
Hence the replayed dense polynomial is the nontrivial constant \(F=1/2\).  Here ``nontrivial'' means that the query is not a sure event: for example, an assignment with \(x_1=0\) and \(x_{k+1}=1\) does not belong to \(B_k\).  The constancy is instead the algebraic cancellation induced by the fair supported row at \(X_1\).

The key \(rstar\) is nevertheless directly relevant to the event-level replay.  Indeed, \(X_{k+1}\) is not intervened upon, the membership test defining \(B_k\) depends on its value, and every event-consistent complete-assignment term in the preceding sum contains exactly one factor \(p_q(x_{k+1})\) labeled by \(rstar\).  Thus the target-relevance field required by the definition of \(Ictx\) labels \(rstar\) as directly event-relevant even though summation cancels \(q\).

It remains to count the records forced by the grammar.  An assignment in \(B_k\) is obtained by choosing the common value \(x_1=x_{k+1}\) in two ways and then choosing \(x_2,\ldots,x_k\) independently in \(2^{k-1}\) ways.  Therefore
\[
 |B_k|=2\cdot 2^{k-1}=2^k.
\]
By the definition of \(Ictx\), its assignment-level portion contains a distinct record for every event-consistent complete target-assignment term.  By \(\texttt{def:checker}\), \(Check\) verifies exhaustive lexicographic indexing of precisely those records and rejects an omitted term.  Hence every \(Ictx\) accepted by \(Check\) on this instance contains at least \(2^k\) assignment records.  The fixed tagged, length-delimited representation in \(\texttt{def:certificate-grammar}\) assigns positive encoded length to every record.  Its output length is therefore \(\Omega(2^k)\).  In the standard sequential bit-cost model, producing that explicit output takes at least its length, and hence also takes \(\Omega(2^k)\) time.

Suppose, for contradiction, that a compiler for this grammar had time and output length bounded by a polynomial in the explicit grounding size and by an exponential factor depending only on \(w\).  Along the constructed family the explicit pre-incidence size is \(O(k)\) and \(w=0\), so the asserted bound would be polynomial in \(k\).  This contradicts the lower bound \(\Omega(2^k)\).  Thus no such width-sensitive guarantee is possible for the present exhaustive assignment-level \(Ictx\) and \(Check\).  The argument does not apply to a replacement circuit-level incidence grammar: as observed in \(\texttt{def:compiler-handle}\), variable elimination may represent the constant polynomial \(1/2\) compactly, while the lower bound proved here arises solely from the current requirement to materialize all event-consistent complete assignments.
